canDos.textEn: Can understand the name and role, etc. of staff members at your new job when they’re introduced to you.
Can give a somewhat detailed self-introduction when you give first greetings at work and other places.
Can talk in simple terms about your hometown.
Can write a simple self-introduction on social media.
Can describe a person’s characteristics or identify a person by listening to their characteristics when you are looking for someone.
Can talk about the traits and appearance of a person who is not present.
Can talk in simple terms about a famous person you like, why you like them and why you first liked them.
Can read a simple interview article and understand the contents.
Can read a menu and understand the names of dishes, prices, and services.
Can tell someone you are dining with or the restaurant staff what you cannot eat and the reasons.
Can tell the restaurant staff your requests for seating, orders, etc.
Can make a restaurant reservation by phone.
Can look at a restaurant coupon and find the necessary information.
Can listen to information about a recommended restaurant and understand its features.
Can listen to and understand the instructions on how to eat a dish.
Can ask or answer questions about how to eat a dish.
Can give a simple explanation about a dish from your country, such as the characteristics, ingredients, and how to eat it.
Can read online reviews about restaurants and find information, such as taste and price.
Can listen to brief information of tourist destinations in Japan and understand what these places are like and what you can do there.
Can discuss travel plans with a friend.
Can ask someone for advice or give them your advice on travel planning.
Can read reviews on a travel site and more or less understand the contents.
Can look at a train ticket, signs on a train, the bulletin board at a station, etc. to find the necessary information.
Can talk in simple terms about your travel plans to a person you met during your trip.
Can listen to the announcements at a station or on the train and get the necessary information or ask questions to someone nearby when you are not sure.
Can talk in simple terms about how your trip was.
Can write a simple post on social media about your experience and impressions of a trip.
Can get the main information from notices on a community bulletin board or in your mailbox, etc.
Can ask questions about community events and notices and understand the answers.
Can listen to an event announcement on a community radio broadcast and understand the main information.
Can ask questions about the content and understand the answers when you are invited to a community event.
Can look at an event program and find the main information, such as the starting time and the performances.
Can ask staff members or others about the time and place of events and understand the answers.
Can ask the person in charge about the requirements for participating in the event you are interested in and how to apply.
Can listen to and more or less understand precautions and other announcements at an event venue.
Can read and understand simple posts on social media written by a friend who participated in the event.
Can write simple posts on social media about the event you participated in.
Can listen to and understand what to do and what to eat, etc. for annual events in Japan.
Can talk in simple terms about what you did during vacation, such as the New Year holidays, and how it was, etc.
Can talk in simple terms about festivals and events in your country.
Can read and more or less understand an article about a local event you participated in.
Can write and send New Year’s greetings.
Can ask about manners and customs for weddings and funerals in Japan and understand the answers.
Can ask and comment about the difference in manners and customs between Japan and your country.
Can talk in simple terms about an event relating to intercultural experiences.
Can read and more or less understand online posts about differences in manners and customs.
Can tell a shop assistant your request about color, size, etc. at a clothing store and buy what you want.
Can tell people nearby about a problem while shopping.
Can describe a lost item and the place you lost it.
Can listen to and more or less understand in-store announcements at, for example, a shopping mall.
Can ask someone which model to buy and where, when you want something.
Can use a flea market application or website to buy electric appliances and other items.
Can look at a product comparison chart and the price tags of electric appliances at an electronics retail store to get the necessary information.
Can ask store staff about a product or ask for a discount when you are buying electric appliances.
Can listen to and understand what there is and what can be done when you are shown around facilities.
Can listen to and understand instructions, such as how to use the gym and other public facilities.
Can ask questions about how to use the library, etc., and understand the answers.
Can read and understand library information written in simple Japanese for non-Japanese residents.
Can look at and understand signs, such as “no photography allowed,” posted in facilities.
Can listen to the instructions and understand how to use delivery, dry cleaning, and other services.
Can read a delivery notice for mail or an express package and understand how to request redelivery.
Can explain your wishes about a hairstyle at a beauty salon or a barber shop.
Can listen to and understand what kind of services are available to non-Japanese residents at the International Exchange Association, etc.
Can look at a notice about eco-friendly activities posted at work, etc. and understand what to be mindful of.
Can talk about things you are mindful of for the environment or listen to and understand what others say.
Can read and understand instructions on how to throw away of garbage, such as when to throw away a certain kind of garbage.
Can ask and understand how to throw away a certain kind of garbage.
Can listen to news and announcements about a disaster and understand what happened and what to do.
Can listen to the explanation and instructions for emergency drills and understand what to do and what to keep in mind.
Can listen to and more or less understand the explanation on what to do in case of earthquakes at emergency drills, etc.
Can ask people around you for the necessary information in case of a disaster.
Can read and understand brochures for disaster prevention written in simple Japanese for non-Japanese residents.
Can talk in simple terms about what you’ve experienced and how life has changed after coming to Japan.
Can talk in simple terms about how your work is going lately to your co-workers.
Can write a simple message about how you are doing lately and send it to your Japanese-language teacher, etc.
Can talk in simple terms about your dreams and hopes.
Can listen to and more or less understand the experience and advice of a person who has lived in Japan for many years.
Can express thanks at a farewell party, etc. referring to some brief episodes.
